name: Software Developer Fellow @ Optivide
summary: Building a cross-platform mobile app with contract-first APIs and AI-assisted delivery workflows for a Google Cloud-backed product.
impact: Shipping React Native features with route-controller-service patterns, spec-first development, and stronger code review quality gates.
description: Build cross-platform mobile product experiences while working across the frontend and API contract layer.

caseStudy.context: Optivide is an active product build where I contribute to a cross-platform mobile app backed by Google Cloud services. The work matters because reliability and delivery quality have to hold up while the product surface is still evolving quickly.
caseStudy.owned: I own user-facing React Native features and contribute to the spec-first workflow around the backend contract. I also use AI intentionally in code review and implementation loops to keep delivery fast without lowering the bar on quality.
caseStudy.constraints: The product is moving quickly, which means features have to fit an established Express route-controller-service architecture and stay aligned with a contract-first API shape instead of becoming one-off frontend patches.
caseStudy.technicalApproach: I build within a typed React Native surface, coordinate against backend contracts early, and rely on GitHub Actions plus structured review loops to catch integration issues before they compound.
caseStudy.outcome: The result is a more dependable shipping process for mobile features: faster iteration, cleaner boundaries between frontend and backend work, and code that is easier for teammates to review and extend.

name: Lead Software Developer @ ENXTI
summary: Leading weekly MVP delivery across a React Native app and Next.js web app for non-technical founders.
impact: Managed a 5-person team while shipping GraphQL, Firebase, Stripe, webhooks, and UX redesign work for growth-ready product flows.
description: Lead developer for a startup MVP spanning mobile, web, and user-management systems.

caseStudy.context: ENXTI needed momentum across both product execution and engineering leadership. The founders were non-technical, so shipping velocity had to be paired with strong translation between product needs and implementation decisions.
caseStudy.owned: I supervised a 5-person developer team, planned weekly feature work, implemented product features myself, and handled parts of the integration surface across GraphQL, MongoDB-style user management concerns, Stripe, and Firebase-backed workflows.
caseStudy.constraints: The MVP had to move quickly across both a React Native app and a Next.js web app, which meant avoiding fragmented decisions and keeping the team aligned around the same product priorities each week.
caseStudy.technicalApproach: I treated the work as both a delivery and coordination problem: breaking features into shippable slices, driving UX redesign decisions, wiring integrations like webhooks and payments, and keeping implementation practical for a small team.
caseStudy.outcome: The team was able to ship weekly product improvements toward an MVP that was more coherent for users and more sustainable for future development.

name: GIS and Software Engineer Volunteer @ LADOT
summary: Automated geospatial model-training workflows for city engineers using Python, Mapillary, and YOLO tooling.
impact: Raised object-detection confidence above 90% and accelerated engineers' workflows by 20% with reusable automation.
description: Supported geospatial engineering workflows with automation and model-training operations.

caseStudy.context: LADOT needed better support for object-detection model training and the repetitive workflow around sourcing and preparing imagery for engineering use.
caseStudy.owned: I administered parts of the model-training workflow, wrote reusable Python automation, and interfaced with the Mapillary API to reduce manual work for engineers.
caseStudy.constraints: The work had to fit existing public-sector workflows, where accuracy mattered and improvements had to be practical for engineers using the outputs downstream.
caseStudy.technicalApproach: I combined Python automation with geospatial tooling and model-training operations, focusing on repeatability so the same steps could be reused instead of manually re-created.
caseStudy.outcome: The workflow became faster and more reliable, with confidence scores pushed above 90% and internal process time improved by roughly 20%.

name: Software Engineer Intern @ TourScout
summary: Revamped customer review-widget creation so a founder could manage embeddable experiences without manual updates.
impact: Built real-time CRUD dashboards and secure Supabase schemas, increasing retention by 40%.
description: Product-focused frontend internship centered on self-serve tooling and real-time updates.

caseStudy.context: TourScout needed more scalable customer tooling so a non-technical founder would not need to manually maintain dynamic review and display experiences.
caseStudy.owned: I redesigned the review-button creation flow, built a real-time information-visualization panel with multi-tenant CRUD functionality, and designed secure Supabase schemas with row-level security.
caseStudy.constraints: The product had to feel easy for non-technical users while still supporting real-time updates and safe access to customer data.
caseStudy.technicalApproach: I focused on user flow clarity first, then connected the frontend to Supabase-backed data operations and real-time updates so the system felt self-serve instead of maintenance-heavy.
caseStudy.outcome: The founder could manage the product with much less manual upkeep, and the resulting dashboard improvements contributed to a 40% increase in retention.

impact: Helped 15 students strengthen Swift fundamentals and ship better assignments with faster unblock time.
description: Teaching and mentorship role for USC's iOS development course.

summary: Coordinated a WordPress relaunch while rebuilding product-data operations for a manufacturing brand.
